properties.title: PSI-117_Analyzed Data_MST_2024_Burning_history_Flame_diameter.csv
properties.summary: Experimental and model histories include squared droplet diameter, flame diameter and radiant power with separate time axes. The source labels model cases as 1 atm with initial diameter 4 mm. Independent column groups must be aligned by their time coordinate, not by file row.

properties.title: PSI-117_Analyzed Data_MST_2024_Dext.csv
properties.summary: The source separates model pressure and hot/cool extinction columns from an experimental pressure and cool-extinction series. Unequal counts are retained; no one-to-one experimental/model matching is inferred from row order.

properties.title: PSI-117_Analyzed Data_MST_2024_Kavg.csv
properties.summary: The source provides separate experimental and model pressure/burning-rate series. The model header specifies mm²/s; the experimental Kavg_CF column does not repeat a unit. Its unit is left unresolved in this graph rather than silently borrowed.

properties.title: PSI-117_Analyzed Data_MST_2024_Radiance_Flame_Diameter.csv
properties.summary: Experimental groups are labelled 0.5 atm and 5 atm with distinct initial diameters. Simulation groups provide radiant power, flame diameter and peak temperature. The source uses Radiance for quantities labelled W; this graph preserves that label but does not reinterpret W as spectral radiance.

properties.title: PSI-117_Analyzed Data_PROCI_2019_Oscillatory_Cool_Flame.csv

Gas-composition entries in the accompanying index mix fractions and percentages and should not be normalized without the corresponding presentation.

properties.title: PSI-117_Analyzed Data_PROCI_2023_Alkane_Extinction_Diameter_1atm.csv

properties.title: PSI-117_Analyzed Data_PROCI_2023_C12_Extinction_Diameter_vs_pressure.csv
properties.summary: Separate experimental and model hot/cool extinction-diameter series indexed by pressure in atm. Additional columns provide upper and lower cool-flame error-bar values. The independent series have unequal lengths and are not joined merely by row number.

properties.title: PSI-117_Analyzed Data_PROCI_C12_2019_Three_Stage.csv
properties.summary: The file places experimental dimensionless-time series, flame dimensions and radiance beside simulation time, droplet diameter, burning rate and peak temperature. Each time axis belongs to its own adjacent series. Experimental and simulation columns are not interchangeable.

properties.title: PSI-117_Presentations_Extinction_Characteristics_TFarouk.pdf
properties.summary: The presentation compares n-heptane, n-decane and n-dodecane simulations with droplet observations. It reports stronger cool-flame reactivity and smaller extinction diameters for longer n-alkanes in the investigated cases. For n-dodecane, pressure changes lead from two-stage burning toward multicycle and warm-flame behavior. Numerical cases and measured comparisons are kept distinct; these trends are conditional on the stated model, fuel and ambient conditions.

properties.title: PSI-117_Presentations_Three_Stage_Cool_Flame_TFarouk.pdf
properties.summary: The presentation reports numerical n-heptane cases in which helium exchange at elevated pressure changes the intermediate and cool burning stages. It describes n-dodecane observations as supporting a prior prediction of three-stage behavior. The warm and cool stages involve different low-temperature kinetic balances; model examples are not represented as additional ISS runs.

evidence.text: The objective of this ground investigation was to use flight data obtained from PSI through NASA’s Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) to quantify how externally imposed thermal and convective perturbations regulated the dynamics and ultimate fate of already established droplet cool flames, and to explain run-to-run variability by isolating the roles of deliberate heating and unintentional drift-induced convection. Focusing on both small and large droplets, the work mapped stability windows for ignition, sustained oscillation, transitions to hot ignition and warm-flame behavior, and extinction under microgravity. By leveraging and extending the FLEX data in the PSI, this study produced reusable models and sensitivity analyses that coupled low-temperature chemistry with transport and radiative effects.

OpenFOAM was used to develop a 3-D CFD model of n-alkane droplet cool flames in microgravity, coupling variable-density Navier–Stokes flow with low-temperature combustion chemistry, coupled heat and mass transfer, and radiation. Model fidelity was established against ISS FLEX measurements, after which controlled simulations examined three forcing modes (i) convection alone to mimic droplet drift, (ii) imposed heat flux, and (iii) combined convection plus heating applied to both large (1–4 mm) and sub-millimeter (~0.5 mm) droplets. To accelerate progress, the study began with simplified chemistry and transitioned to reduced mechanisms for parameter sweeps over forcing amplitude and frequency, ambient composition (including ozone-assisted cases), and pressure. From each case, predictive observables were extracted (ignition delay, oscillation frequency and amplitude, stand-off and extinction diameters), and were used to construct stability maps that delineated conditions for cool-flame onset, persistence, and quenching. These maps were reconciled with FLEX observations and were used to guide next-generation test matrices for both large- and small-droplet experiments.
